$comment: Brand-neutral reasons for putting graphics on screen. A brand pack maps these stable editorial intents to its own roles, components, priorities, and visual treatment.

intents.identify: Identify a person, channel, product, or segment without interrupting the source.
intents.caption: Make spoken language readable or accessible in sync with speech.
intents.preview: Promise or preview what the viewer is about to receive.
intents.structure: Expose the current topic or structural boundary.
intents.enumerate: Make a spoken sequence, agenda, or process easier to follow.
intents.emphasize: Strengthen a genuinely important spoken beat without adding a new claim.
intents.explain: Add context, a definition, model, or relationship that narration alone leaves unclear.
intents.compare: Make a meaningful contrast between options, states, or evidence explicit.
intents.quantify: Make a verified number, result, or distribution legible.
intents.cite: Attribute a claim, quotation, or source.
intents.instruct: Direct attention to an action, control, shortcut, or prompt.
intents.show-state: Expose a system, agent, or workflow state.
intents.navigate: Orient the viewer in chapters, progress, or what comes next.
intents.transition: Bridge real structural sections of the video.
intents.warn: Call out a literal risk, constraint, or failure that needs special attention.
intents.call-to-action: Offer an explicit next action when the narration supports it.
intents.disclose: Show required commercial or editorial disclosure.
intents.error: Make an actual broken or failed state visible.
intents.unavailable: Preserve historical inventory without making it selectable.
